prompt: A location service keeps only each connected driver’s latest position. Drivers start reporting twice as often, but their count and record sizes stay the same. What changes?

options.explanation: Wrong. Each driver still has one current record; the record is replaced more often.

options.text: Update work rises while the raw latest-record count stays the same
options.explanation: Correct. Reporting rate controls ingestion; driver count controls the number of current records.
Wrong. A location ping is not a request for a new trip.

options.text: Retaining every historical ping costs the same as retaining one position
options.explanation: Wrong. Historical samples accumulate and need a separate retention budget.

workedExample: Follow one driver: the new ping replaces their previous current position. More frequent pings increase validation, network and index work without adding current drivers. If every ping is archived, history grows faster even though the current-state index does not.
